positions.as_written: Phase boundaries are defined by events that themselves must be detected, so subphase timings differ between laboratories.
Read a flattened stance flexion wave as quadriceps inhibition until proved otherwise.
Measure stance time symmetry, which is the cheapest reliable asymmetry marker available.
Avoid averaging a moment across stance, since the knee's moments reverse within it.
Speed, which must be matched before any two stance measurements are compared.
Assess the stance flexion wave by observation and treat its absence as significant, since nothing in clinic measures it.
Report a moment curve rather than a peak when one is available.
Expect a lost flexion wave to raise loading rate, which is a mechanical argument for restoring it rather than working around it.
